topic: Most goals in men's FIFA World Cup history: Kylian Mbappé, 22, after the 2026 tournament (10 in 2026, Golden Boot); passed Lionel Messi (21) with two goals in the third-place playoff v England in Miami Gardens on 18 July 2026 (England won 6–4); Messi passed Miroslav Klose's 16 (held since 2014) in June 2026 and led for about a month; Ronaldo (Brazil) 15
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Klose still holds the World Cup scoring record with 16.
myths.reality: The 2026 tournament rewrote it: Messi passed 16 in June, finished on 21; Mbappé finished on 22 and is now the all-time leader.
